newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila money mkt on sell side after rate declines.
newsitem.headline: Manila money mkt on sell side after rate declines.

text.p: The secondary market of Philippine Treasury bills was swamped with sellers after rates fell in the auction, traders said on Tuesday.
"Everybody thinks it's time to sell since the Central Bank's overnight rate is still at 14 percent," a foreign bank dealer.
Banks would rather invest their money in the Central Bank's term reverse repos where the rates are still higher, he said.
"(But) there was no buyer. There was no real demand for the bills," a second trader said.
A Reuters poll of eight financial institutions gave offers of 10.10/10.25 percent for the three-month bills; 10.40/10.50 percent for the six months; and 10.75/10.90 for the one-year bills.
On the auction of the two-year Treasury bond, traders said the coupon rate could go down to 11.375 to 11.75 percent from the previous rate of 12 percent due to the high liquidity in the system.
Meanwhile, the interbank call loan rate remained at an average of 14.03125 percent, with 27 lenders and 19 borrowers.
Volume fell to 11.53 billion pesos from 12.66 billion.
